title: Trump Backtracks on Plan for New Controls on N.I.H. Grants
summary: Democrats and Republicans in Congress opposed the creation of a commission with the power to veto federal research awards.

The White House has backed away from a plan to issue an executive order that would subject billions of dollars in federal health and biomedical research spending to heightened political scrutiny, according to four people familiar with the situation.


The proposed directive would have established a commission with the power to block government research grants if the money supported work in areas that did not align with President Trump’s political agenda. The plan was discussed in a White House meeting on Friday, and some on Capitol Hill had expected Mr. Trump to issue the order as soon as this week.


But fierce opposition from both Democrats and Republicans in Congress forced the White House to recalibrate this week, according to some of the people familiar with the discussions, who described private conversations on the condition of anonymity. Nevertheless, they said, officials do not appear to have totally abandoned their desire to tighten their grip over federal research spending,


The White House, its Office of Management and Budget and the National Institutes of Health either did not respond to requests for comment, or declined to comment. The status of the order was[reported earlier by Semafor](https://www.semafor.com/article/09/23/2026/trump-administration-backing-off-nih-grant-order-amid-pushback) .


At the heart of the matter is the N.I.H., the nation’s largest research agency, which disburses much of its $48 billion annual budget to


researchers who study cancer, infectious diseases and other health priorities.


Historically, the N.I.H. has awarded these grants based on scientific merit after a rigorous review by experts in the relevant fields. But under Mr. Trump, political appointees have exerted extraordinary control over the grant-making process in a bid to eliminate spending seen as “woke,” and to exert pressure on Harvard University and other elite universities that the president[accuses of antisemitism and liberal indoctrination](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/05/04/us/politics/trump-ivy-league.html) .
